verifiedTakeaway.symptom: Websites take 2 to 4 seconds before starting to load
verifiedTakeaway.rootCause: ISP DNS resolver queue backlog or negative cache TTL lock
verifiedTakeaway.instantFix: Switch network adapter IPv4 DNS to 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8 and flush DNS cache

howToSteps.name: Flush the Local Windows DNS Resolver Cache
howToSteps.text: Open Terminal or PowerShell as Administrator and run the flush command.
howToSteps.proTip: Make sure you see 'Successfully flushed the DNS Resolver Cache'.

sections.heading: Why DNS Lookups Stall Your Connection
paragraphs: Before your browser downloads the first byte of a webpage, it must resolve the domain name to an IP address.
If your default router DNS relay is congested, switching to a high-speed Anycast resolver resolves domains in under 20 milliseconds.

faqs.question: Does flushing DNS delete any saved passwords?
faqs.answer: No. It only clears the temporary table of mapped hostnames and IP addresses.
